name: Antipater of Thessalonica
bio: Antipater of Thessalonica wrote in the Augustan age and belongs to the Garland of Philippus. He addressed Roman patrons, among them Lucius Calpurnius Piso, in epigrams of many kinds.
Only epigrams headed “Antipater of Thessalonica” in Paton's volume are filed here.

poems.title: Book V, 3
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: The day has broken, Chrysilla, and for long early-rising chanticleer is crowing to summon envious Dawn. A curse on thee, most jealous of fowls, who drivest me from home to the tireless chatter of the young men. Thou art growing old, Tithonus, or why dost thou chase thy consort Aurora so early from thy bed?

poems.title: Book V, 30
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: All Homer says is well said, but this most excellently that Aphrodite is golden. For if, my friend, you bring the coin, there is neither a porter in the way, nor a dog chained before the door. But if you come without it, there is Cerberus himself there. Oh! grasping code of wealth, how dost thou oppress poverty !

poems.title: Book V, 31
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Formerly there were three ages, a golden, a silver, and a brazen, but Cytherea is now all three. She honours the man of gold, and she kisses the brazen man and she never turns her back on the silver men. She is a very Nestor?; I even think that Zeus came to Danae, not turned to gold, but bringing a hundred gold sovereigns.

poems.title: Book V, 109
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: You can have the Attic Europa for a drachma with none to fear and no opposition on her part, and she has perfectly clean sheets and a fire in winter. T was quite superfluous for you, dear Zeus, to turn into a bull.

poems.title: Book VI, 198
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Lycon, having shaved the down that flowered in its season under his temples, the manly ornament of his cheeks, dedicated it to Phoebus, a first gift, and therewith prayed that so he might also shave the gray hairs from his temples. Grant him an old age such as his youth, and as thou hast made him now thus, may he remain thus when the snow of hoary eld falls on his head.

poems.title: Book VII, 18: On Aleman
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Do not judge the man by the stone. Simple is the tomb to look on, but holds the bones of a great man, Thou shalt know Aleman the supreme striker of the Laconian lyre, possessed by the nine Muses. Here resteth he, a cause of dispute to two continents, if he be a Lydian or a Spartan. Minstrels have many mothers.

poems.title: Book VII, 39: On Aeschylus
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Here, far from the Attic land, making Sicily glorious by his tomb, lies Aeschylus, son of Euphorion, who first built high with massive eloquence the diction of tragedy and its beetling song.

poems.title: Book VII, 168
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: “Let women after this pray for children,” cried Polyxo, her belly torn by three babes; and in the midwife’s hands she fell dead, while the boys slid from her hollow flanks to the ground, a live birth from a dead mother. So one god took life from her and gave it to them.

poems.title: Book VII, 185
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: The Italian earth holds me an African, and near to Rome I lie, a virgin yet, by these sands. Pompeia who reared me wept for me as for a daughter and laid me in a freewoman’s grave. Another light she hoped for, but this came earlier, and the torch was lit not as we prayed, but by Persephone.

poems.title: Book VII, 216
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: The waves and rough surges drove me, the dolphin, on the land, a spectacle of misfortune for all strangers to look on. Yet on earth pity finds a place, for the men who saw me straightway in reverence decked me for my grave. But now the sea who bore me has destroyed me. What faith is there in the sea, that spared not even her own nursling?

poems.title: Book VII, 236
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I, this Magnesian tomb, am not that of Themistocles, but I was built as a record of the envious misjudgment of the Greeks.”

poems.title: Book VII, 286
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Unhappy Nicanor, wasted by the grey sea, thou liest naked on a strange beach or perchance near the rocks; gone from thee are thy rich halls, and the hope of all Tyre has perished. None of thy possessions saved thee; alas, poor wight, thou art dead and hast laboured but for the fishes and the sea.

poems.title: Book VII, 287
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Even in death shall the unappeased sea vex me, Lysis, buried as I am beneath this desert rock, sounding ever harshly in my ears close to my deaf tomb. Why, O men, did ye lay me next to her who reft me of breath, who wrecked me not trading on a merchantman, but embarked on a little rowing-boat? From the sea I sought to gain my living, and from the sea I drew forth death.

poems.title: Book VII, 288
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I belong entirely to neither now I am dead, but sea and land possess an equal portion of me. My flesh the fishes ate in the sea, but my bones have been washed up on this cold beach.

poems.title: Book VII, 289
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: When shipwrecked Antheus had swum ashore at night on a small plank to the mouth of the Peneus, a solitary wolf rushing from the thicket slew him off his guard. O waves less treacherous than the land!

poems.title: Book VII, 367
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Say that I am the corpse of Italian Egerius whose eyes when he went to meet his bride were veiled by a dim cloud, which extinguished his life together with his eyesight, after he had but seen the girl. Alas, O Sun, that heaven allotted him such a fate! Cursed be that envious wedding torch, whether unwilling Hymen lit or willing Hades.

poems.title: Book VII, 369
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I am the tomb of the orator Antipater. Ask all Greece to testify to his inspiration. He lies here, and men dispute whether his birth was from Athens or from Egypt; but he was worthy of both continents. For the matter of that, the lands are of one blood, as Greek legend says, but the one is ever allotted to Pallas and the other to Zeus.

poems.title: Book VII, 390
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: You have heard of Cyllene the Arcadian mountain. That is the monument that covers Apollodorus. As he journeyed from Pisa by night the thunderbolt from Zeus killed him; and far from Aeanae and Beroea” the racer sleeps, conquered by Zeus.

poems.title: Book VII, 398
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I know not whether to blame Bacchus or the rain; both are treacherous for the feet. For this tomb holds Polyxenus who once, returning from the country after a banquet, fell from the slippery hill-side. Far from Aeolian Smyrna he lies. Let everyone at night when drunk dread the rain-soaked path.

poems.title: Book VII, 402
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: On the winter snow melting at the top of her house it fell in and killed old Lysidice. Her neighbours of the village did not make her a tomb of earth dug up for the purpose, but put her house itself over her as a tomb.

poems.title: Book VII, 493
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I, Rhodope, and my mother Boisca neither died of sickness, nor fell by the sword of the foes, but ourselves, when dreadful Ares burnt the city of Corinth our country, chose a brave death. My mother slew me with the slaughtering knife, nor did she, unhappy woman, spare her own life, but tied the noose round her neck; for it was better than slavery to die in freedom.

poems.title: Book VII, 530: On Niobe and her children
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Thou ferry-man of the dead, receive me, who could not hold my tongue, alone with my children; a boat-load from the house of Tantalus is sufficient for thee. One womb shall fill thy boat; look on my boys and girls, the spoils of Phoebus and Artemis.

poems.title: Book VII, 531
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: The very mother who bore thee, Demetrius, gave thee death when forgetful of thy duty thou didst fly, driving the’ sword into thy flanks. Holding the steel that reeked with her son’s blood, gnashing her teeth, foaming at the mouth, and looking askance like a Spartan woman as she was, she exclaimed “Leave the Eurotas; go to Tartarus. Since thou couldst fly like a coward, thou art neither mine nor Sparta’s.

poems.title: Book VII, 629
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Dost thou who art so great rest in so shallow a soil? He who looks at thee, Socrates, must blame the unwisdom of the Greeks. Merciless judges who slew the best of men, nor shamed them one jot. Such often are the Athenians.

poems.title: Book VII, 637
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Pyrrhus the solitary oarsman, fishing with his hair-line for small hakes and sprats from his little boat, fell, struck by a thunderbolt, far away from the shore. The boat came ashore of itself, bearing the message by sulphur and smoke, and had no need of a speaking keel like that of Argo.

poems.title: Book VII, 639
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Every sea is sea. Why do we foolishly blame the Cyclades, or the Hellespont, and the Sharp Isles? They merit not their evil fame; for why, when I had escaped them, did the harbour of Scarphaea drown me? Let who will pray for fair weather to bring him home; Aristagoras, who is buried here, knows that the sea is the sea.

poems.title: Book VII, 640
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Fearsome for sailors is the setting of the Kids, but for Pyro calm was far more adverse than storm. For his ship, stayed by calm, was overtaken by a swift double-oared pirate galley. He was slain by them, having escaped the storm but to perish in the calm. Alas, in what an evil harbour ended his voyage!

poems.title: Book VII, 666
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: This is the place where Leander crossed, these are the straits, unkind not only to one lover. This is where Hero once dwelt, here are the ruins of the tower, the treacherous lamp rested here. In this tomb they both repose, still reproaching that envious wind.

poems.title: Book VII, 692
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.note: Attribution doubtful in Paton (Antipater or Philip of Thessalonica).
poems.text: Glyco of Pergamus, the glory of Asia, the thunderbolt of the pancration, the broad-footed, the new Atlas, has perished; they have perished, those unvanquished hands, and Hades, who conquers all, has thrown him who never before met with a fall in Italy, Greece, or Asia.

poems.title: Book VII, 705: Not Sepulchral
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Amphipolis, tomb of Edonian Phyllis, washed by the Strymon and great Hellespont, all that is left of thee is the ruin of the temple of Brauronian Artemis and the disputed water of thy river. We see her for whom the Athenians strove so long now lying like a torn rag of precious purple on either bank,

poems.title: Book IX, 3
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: They planted me, a walnut-tree, by the road-side to amuse passing boys, as a mark for their well-aimed stones. And all my twigs and flourishing shoots are broken, hit as I am by showers of pebbles. It is no advantage for trees to be fruitful. I indeed, poor tree, bore fruit only for my own undoing.

poems.title: Book IX, 10
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: An octopus once, stretched out on a rock that projected into the sea, extended his many feet to let them bask in the sun. He had not yet changed to the colour of the rock, and therefore a sharp-eyed eagle saw him from the clouds and seized him, but fell, unhappy bird, entangled by his tentacles, into the sea, losing both its prey and its life.

poems.title: Book IX, 26
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: These are the divine-voiced women that Helicon fed with song, Helicon and Macedonian Pieria’s rock: Praxilla; Moero; Anyte, the female Homer; Sappho, glory of the Lesbian women with lovely tresses; Erinna; renowned Telesilla; and thou, Corinna, who didst sing the martial shield of Athena; Nossis, the tender-voiced, and dulcet-toned Myrtis— all craftswomen of eternal pages. Great Heaven gave birth to nine Muses, and Earth to these ten, the deathless delight of men.

poems.title: Book IX, 46
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: A blind and childless woman, who prayed that she might either recover her sight or bear a child, gained both blessings. For not long after she was brought to bed, as she never had expected, and on the same day saw the sweet light of day for which she had longed with all her heart. Both her prayers were heard by Artemis, the deliverer in child-bed and the bearer of the white-rayed torch.

poems.title: Book IX, 59
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Four Victories, winged, hold aloft on their backs as many of the immortals. One uplifts Athena in her warlike guise, one Aphrodite, one Heracles, and another dauntless Ares. They are painted on the fair dome of thy house, and mount to heaven. O Caius, bulwark of thy country, Rome, may Heracles, the devourer of oxen, make thee invincible; may Cypris bless thee with a good wife, Pallas endue thee with wisdom, and Ares with fearlessness.

poems.title: Book IX, 72
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Hermes, ye shepherds, is easily contented, rejoicing in libations of milk and honey from the oak-tree, but not so Heracles. He demands a ram or fat lamb, or in any case a whole victim. But he keeps off the wolves. What profits that, when the sheep he protects if not slain by the wolf is slain by its protector ?

poems.title: Book IX, 77
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Hera, tortured by the beauty of Ganymede, and with the soul-consuming sting of jealousy in her heart, once spoke thus: “Troy gave birth to a male flame for Zeus; therefore I will send a flame to fall on Troy, Paris the bringer of woe. No eagle shall come again to the Trojans, but vultures to the feast, the day that the Danai gather the spoils of their labour.”

poems.title: Book IX, 82
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Trust not, mariner, to the fatal sea, even when thou art at anchor, even when thy hawsers are fast on land. For Ion fell overboard in the harbour, and his active hands, fettered by the wine, were useless for swimming. Shun dances and carousal on board ship. The sea is the enemy of Bacchus. Such is the law established by the Tyrrhene pirates.

poems.title: Book IX, 92
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: A little dew is enough to make the cicadas tipsy, but when they have drunk they sing louder than swans. So can the singer who has received hospitality repay his benefactors with song for their little gifts. Therefore first I send thee these lines of thanks, and if the Fates consent thou shalt be often written in my pages.

poems.title: Book IX, 93
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Antipater sends to Piso for his birthday a little volume, the work of one night. Let Piso receive it favourably and praise the poet, like great Zeus, whose favour is often won by a little frankincense.

poems.title: Book IX, 96
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Artigenes of Gela, when he was already on his road to Hades, spoke thus to his daughter: “Maiden with lovely cheeks, daughter mine, let thy spindle ever be thy fellow-worker, a possession sufficient for a life of poverty. But if thou enterest into wedlock, keep with thee the virtues of thy Achaean mother, the safest dowry thy husband can have.”

poems.title: Book IX, 112
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: The astrologers foretold that I would live thrice ten and twice three years, but I am satisfied with the three decades. For this is the right limit of men’s life. Longer life is for Nestor, and even Nestor went to Hades.’

poems.title: Book IX, 149
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Aristides the . . . had not much from many sources, but his fortune was one ewe and one cow. Yet, notwithstanding his poverty, he escaped not Envy, and in one and the same day wild beasts killed the sheep and a difficult birth the cow. Hating the sight of his yard, in which the sound of bleating was silent, he hanged himself by the strap of his wallet from this wild pear-tree.

poems.title: Book IX, 150
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: But the wealth of Aristides was one heifer and one fleecy sheep. By their means he kept famine from the door. But he lost both; a wolf killed the sheep and the cow perished in labour. His poor stock was gone, and noosing his neck in the strap of his wallet, the wretched man died close to his cabin, which no longer echoed to the sound of lowing.

poems.title: Book IX, 186
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: These are the volumes of Aristophanes, a divine work, over which the ivy of Acharnae shook in profusion its green locks. Look how the pages are steeped in Dionysus, how deep-voiced are the dramas full of terrible grace. O comic poet, high of heart, and worthy interpreter of the spirit of Hellas, hating what deserved hate, and mocking where mockery was due! OT

poems.title: Book IX, 215
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Ever, stranger, is the water of Hellespont cruel to women. Ask Cleonike of Dyrrhachium. For she was sailing to Sestos to meet her bridegroom, and in the black ship she met with the same fate as Helle. Poor Hero, thou didst lose a husband, and Deimachus a bride, in the space of a few furlongs.

poems.title: Book IX, 231
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I am a dry plane-tree covered by the vine that climbs over me; and JI, who once fed clusters from my own branches, and was no less leafy than this vine, now am clothed in the glory of foliage not my own. Such a mistress let a man cherish who, unlike her kind, knows how to requite him even when he is dead.

poems.title: Book IX, 238
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Apollo is a big boy here in this bronze work of Onatas which testifies to the beauty of Leto and Zeus, and proclaims that not idly did Zeus love her, and that, even as the saying is, the eyes and head of the son of Cronos are glorious. Not even Hera will be displeased with this bronze which Onatas moulded to such beauty by the help of Ilithyia.’

poems.title: Book IX, 241
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: You were a neat-herd, Phoebus, and Poseidon was a nag, Zeus was a swan, and famous Ammon a snake ? (they did it for the sake of girls, but you, Apollo, were after a boy), all to conceal your identity; for you all enjoy by force and not by persuasion. Evagoras, however, being made of brass, need practise no deceit, but in his own form, and without any transformation, possesses all and every of either sex.

poems.title: Book IX, 266
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Phoebus spoke thus of the sweet musician Glaphyrus when he breathed the spirit of love from his pierced flute: “Marsyas, thou didst lie concerning thy invention, for this man hath stolen Athena’s flute from Phrygia. If thou hadst then breathed into such as this, Hyagnis had never wept for the contest by the Maeander in which the flute was fatal.”

poems.title: Book IX, 268
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Gorgo, the Cretan bitch, being in pup, was on the track of a hind, and had paid her vows to both Dianas. As she killed the deer she littered, and quickly did the Deliveress grant both prayers, that for success in the chase and that for an easy labour. Now Gorgo gives milk to nine children. Fly, ye Cretan deer, learning from the force of mothers in travail what their young are like to be.

poems.title: Book IX, 269
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: When the ship was dashed to pieces two men strove with each other in the water, quarrelling for one plank. Antagoras struck Pisistratus. It was not inexcusable, for his life was at stake, but Justice was concerned. The one swam on, but the other was seized by a shark. She, the all-avenger, does not cease from vengeance even in the watery deep.

poems.title: Book IX, 282
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Strangers, I, whom you take for a tree, am a maiden.’ Bid the slaves’ hands that are prepared to cut me spare the laurel. Instead of me, let travellers cut to strew as a couch boughs of arbutus or terebinth, for they are not far away. The brook is about a hundred yards away from me, and from its springs a wood containing every kind of tree is distant about seventy yards.

poems.title: Book IX, 297: Probably addressed to Gaius Caesar when sent by Augustus to the East in the year 1 B.C.
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Hie thee to the Euphrates, son of Zeus; already in the East the feet of the Parthians hasten to desert to thee. Hie thee on thy way, O prince, and thou shalt find, Caesar, their bow-strings relaxed by fear. But base all thou dost on thy father’s instructions. The Ocean is Rome’s boundary on every side; be thou the first to seal her domination with the rising Sun.

poems.title: Book IX, 302
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Bees, ye savage pack, ye killed baby Hermonax as he was creeping to your hive in quest of honey. Often had he been fed by you, and now, alas! ye have stung him to death. If we speak evil of serpents’ nests, learn from Lysidice and Amyntor not to praise hives either. They, too, have in them bitter honey.

poems.title: Book IX, 305
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I had drunk my fill of untempered water, when Bacchus yesterday, standing by my bed, spoke thus: “Thou sleepest a sleep worthy of them whom Aphrodite hates. Tell me, thou temperate man, hast thou heard of Hippolytus? Fear lest thou suffer some fate such as his.” Having so spoken he departed, and ever since then water is not agreeable to me.

poems.title: Book IX, 309
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: As Gorgo was lighting the coals on her hearth in winter, the fearful noise of the thunder terrified the old woman. Chill seized her lungs and she dropped dead. So then she had been spared with Eld on the one side and Death on the other, either ready to take her on any pretext.

poems.title: Book IX, 407
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: The slave-child of Hippocrates, having crept from the neighbouring cottage to the broad edge of the sea, died of drinking more than it had drunk at the breast. Out on thee, Sea, who didst receive the baby as a mother, and didst deceive it !

poems.title: Book IX, 408
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Would I had continued to stray at the will of all the winds that blow, rather than be fixed firm to help wandering Leto in her labour: I should never have had to lament such solitude. Alas, poor me, how many Greek ships now sail past deserted Delos, once so revered! Hera has taken this late but terrible vengeance on Leto.

poems.title: Book IX, 417
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Lampo, Midas’ hound, died of thirst, though he toiled hard for his life. For with his paws he dug into the damp earth, but the lazy water would not hasten to gush from the hidden source. He fell exhausted, and then the spring burst forth. Is it, Nymphs, that ye were wrath with Lampo for all the deer he had killed ?

poems.title: Book IX, 418: On a Water-mill
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Cease from grinding, ye women who toil at the mill; sleep late, even if the crowing cocks announce the dawn. For Demeter has ordered the Nymphs to perform the work of your hands, and they, leaping down on the top of the wheel, turn its axle which, with its revolving spokes, turns the heavy concave Nisyrian mill-stones. We taste again the joys of the primitive life, learning to feast on the products of Demeter without labour.

poems.title: Book IX, 420
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Think not, Telembrotus, to persuade love by tears, or with a little water to put out so stubborn a fire. Gold is ever the medicine of love, and not even then when he was born on the deep sea was he quenched.

poems.title: Book IX, 421: On the Cyclades
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Ye desert islands, crumbs of land, which the sounding cincture of the Aegean wave confines, ye have followed the example of Siphnus and squalid Pholegandrus, poor islands, and lost your ancient splendour. Delos, of a truth, once so brilliant, has taught you her ways, Delos who first of you all was condemned to solitude.

poems.title: Book IX, 428: Addressed to L. Calpurnius Piso
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Thessalonica, the mother of all Macedonia, sends me to thee, despoiler of Thrace. I sing thy conquest of the martial Bessi, collecting all that I learnt about the war. But be thou, like a god, attentive to me, and listen to my prayers. What occupation is there which can deny an ear to the Muses?

poems.title: Book IX, 517
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Orpheus charmed beasts and thou charmest Orpheus. Phoebus vanquished the Phrygian, but he yields to thee when thou playest, Glaphyrus—the name?‘suits both thy art and thy person. Athena would never have thrown the flute away had she made such music as thou, master of varied delight. Sleep himself, lying in Pasithea’s arms, would awake if he heard thee.

poems.title: Book IX, 541
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Theogenes sends to Piso the skilfully wrought bowls, and both of us together contain the heavens. We are both carved out of a sphere, and one of us contains the southern constellations, the other the northern. No longer consult Aratus, for if you empty us both you see all the Phaenomena.

poems.title: Book IX, 550
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I say not, Tenos, that thou art not famous, for of old the winged sons of Boreas got thee renown. But Ortygia was celebrated too, and her name reached to the Rhipaean Hyperboreans. But now thou livest and she is dead. Who would have expected to see Delos more desert than Tenos ? ?

poems.title: Book IX, 552
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: A sword made of Macedonian steel and taught valiance by the hand of Alexander, I come, Piso,’ longing for thy hand, and thus I greet thee: “I rejoice to find the right hand for which fate reserved me.”

poems.title: Book IX, 557
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Tarsus, Cilician city, the runner Aries, son of Menecles, does not disgrace even Perseus, thy founder. Such are the boy’s winged feet that not even Perseus would have shown him his back in the race. The youth is seen only at the start and the finish, never in the middle of the course.

poems.title: Book IX, 706
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I ama holy tree. Beware of injuring me as thou passest by, stranger, for I suffer pain if I am mutilated. Remember that my bark is still virginal, not like that of savage wild pear-trees. Who does not know what the race of poplars is like? If thou dost bark me, as I stand here by the road, thou shalt weep for it. Though I am but wood, the Sun cares for me.

poems.title: Book X, 25
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Phoebus, guardian of the Cephallenians’ harbour, dwelling on the beach of Panormus that faces rough Ithaca, grant that I may sail to the Asian land through favouring waves in the wake of Piso’s lang ship. And attune my doughty emperor to be kind to him and kind to my verses.

poems.title: Book XI, 20
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Away with you who sing of loccae! (cloaks) or lophnides! (torches) or camasenes! (fish), race of thorn-gathering poets; and you who practising effeminately decorative verse drink only simple water from the holy fount. To-day we pour the wine in honour of the birthday of Archilochus and virile Homer. Our bowl receives no water-drinkers.

poems.title: Book XI, 31
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I preap not the setting of the Pleiads, nor the waves of the sea that roar round the stubborn rock, nor the lightning of great heaven so much as I dread a wicked man and water-drinkers who remember all our words.

poems.title: Book XI, 327
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Lycaenis with the dry back, the disgrace of Aphrodite, with less haunches than any deer, with whom, as the saying is, a drunken goatherd would not live. G-r-r, g-r-r such are the wives of the Sidonians.

poems.title: Book XVI, 75
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: Son of Kings, like to Zeus, Apollo, and Ares, lovely offspring granted to a mother’s prayers, from the Fates all kingly, all perfect things have come to thee, and thou art become the theme of Poets. Zeus has his royal sceptre, Ares his spear, and Phoebus his beauty, but thine, Cotys, are all three together.

poems.title: Book XVI, 131: On the Same
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: This is the daughter of Tantalus, who of old bore from a single womb twice seven children, victims of Phoebus and Artemis: for the Maiden sent untimely death to the maiden, the male god to the boys, the two slaying two companies of seven. She, once the mother of such a flock, the mother of lovely children, was not left with one to tend her age. The mother was not, as was meet, buried by her children, but the children all were carried by their mother to the sorrowful tomb. Tantalus, thy tongue was fatal to thee and to thy daughter; she became a rock, and over thee hangs a stone to terrify thee.

poems.title: Book XVI, 143: On the Picture of the Same
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: This is the picture of Medea. See how one eye is raised in wrath, but the other is softened by affection for her children.

poems.title: Book XVI, 184: On another Statue of the Same
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text: I, Dionysus, the fellow-soldier of Italian Piso, am set here to guard his house and bring him good fortune. A worthy house hast thou entered, Dionysus. Meet is the house for Bacchus, and Bacchus for the house.

poems.title: At Cockcrowing (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Grey dawn is over, Chrysilla, and ere now the morning cock clarisoning leads on the envious Lady of Morn. Be thou accursed, most envious of birds, who drivest me from my home to the endless chattering of the young men. Thou growest old, Tithonus; else why dost thou chase Dawn thy bedfellow out of her couch while yet morning is so young?

poems.title: On the Same (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Ausonian earth holds me a woman of Libya, and I lie a maiden here by the sea-sand near Rome; and Pompeia, who nurtured me like a daughter, wept over me and laid me in a free tomb, while hastening on that other torch-fire for me; but this one came first, and contrary to our prayers Persephone lit the lamp.

poems.title: Glaphyrus the Flute-Player (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Phoebus said over clear-voiced Glaphyrus as he breathed desire through the pierced lotus-pipes, "O Marsyas, thou didst tell false of thy discovery, for this is he who carried off Athena's flutes out of Phrygia; and if thou hadst blown then in such as his, Hyagnis would not have wept that disastrous flute-strife by Maeander."

poems.title: The Wife's Prayer (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Cythera of Bithynia dedicated me, the marble image of thy form, O Cyprian, having vowed it: but do thou impart in return thy great grace for this little one, as is thy wont; and concord with her husband satisfies her.

poems.title: A Story of the Sea (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Once on a time when a ship was shattered at sea, two men fell at strife fighting for one plank. Antagoras struck away Pisistratus; one could not blame him, for it was for his life; but Justice took cognisance. The other swam ashore; but him a dog-fish seized; surely the Avenger of the Fates rests not even in the watery deep.

poems.title: Delos (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Would I were yet blown about by ever-shifting gales, rather than fixed for wandering Leto's childbed; I had not so bemoaned my desolation. Ah miserable me, how many Greek ships sail by me, desert Delos, once so worshipful: late, but terrible, is Hera's vengeance laid on me thus for Leto's sake.

poems.title: Amphipolis (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: City built upon Strymon and the broad Hellespont, grave of Edonian Phyllis, Amphipolis, yet there remain left to thee the traces of the temple of her of Aethopion and Brauron, and the water of the river so often fought around; but thee, once the high strife of the sons of Aegeus, we see like a torn rag of sea-purple on either shore.

poems.title: Drowned in Harbour (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Not even when at anchor trust the baleful sea, O sailor, nor even if dry land hold thy cables; for Ion fell into the harbour, and at the plunge wine tied his quick sailor's hands. Beware of revelling on ship-board; the sea is enemy to Iacchus; this law the Tyrrhenians ordained.

poems.title: In Sound of the Sea (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Even in death shall the implacable sea vex me, Lysis hidden beneath a lonely rock, ever sounding harshly by my ear and alongside of my deaf tomb. Why, O fellow-men, have you made my dwelling by this that reft me of breath, me whom not trading in my merchant-ship but sailing in a little rowing-boat, it brought to shipwreck? and I who sought my living out of the sea, out of the sea likewise drew my death.

poems.title: The Empty House (Mackail)
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Hapless Nicanor, doomed by the grey sea, thou liest then naked on a strange beach, or haply by the rocks, and those wealthy halls are perished from thee, and lost is the hope of all Tyre; nor did aught of thy treasures save thee; alas, pitiable one! thou didst perish, and all thy labour was for the fishes and the sea.

poems.title: A Grave at Ostia
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Ausonian earth contains me
  That was a Libyan maid,
And in the sea's sand hard by Rome
  My virgin form was laid.
Pompeia with a mother's care
  Watched o'er my tender years,
Entombed me here among the free,
  And gave me many tears.
Not as she prayed the torch was fired,
  She would have burned for me;
The lamp which took the torch's place
  Was thine, Persephone.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.3: ὄρθρος ἔβη, Χρύσιλλα, πάλαι δʼ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ὄρθρος ἔβη, Χρύσιλλα, πάλαι δʼ ἠῷος ἀλέκτωρ
κηρύσσων φθονερὴν Ἠριγένειαν ἄγει.
ὀρνίθων ἔρροις φθονερώτατος, ὅς με διώκεις
οἴκοθεν εἰς πολλοὺς ἠιθέων ὀάρους.
γηράσκεις, Τιθωνέ· τί γὰρ σὴν εὐνέτιν Ἠῶ
οὕτως ὀρθριδίην ἤλασας ἐκ λεχέων;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.30: πάντα καλῶς, τό γε μήν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
πάντα καλῶς, τό γε μήν, χρυσῆν ὅτι τὴν Ἀφροδίτην,
ἔξοχα καὶ πάντων εἶπεν ὁ Μαιονίδας.
ἢν μὲν γὰρ τὸ χάραγμα φέρῃς, φίλος, οὔτε θυρωρὸς
ἐν ποσίν, οὔτε κύων ἐν προθύροις δέδεται·
ἢν δʼ ἑτέρως ἔλθῃς, καὶ ὁ Κέρβερος. ὦ πλεονέκται,
οἱ πλούτου, πενίην ὡς ἀδικεῖτε νόμοι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.31: χρύσεος ἦν γενεὴ καὶ χάλκεος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
χρύσεος ἦν γενεὴ καὶ χάλκεος ἀργυρέη τε
πρόσθεν· παντοίη δʼ ἡ Κυθέρεια τανῦν,
καὶ χρυσοῦν τίει, καὶ χάλκεον ἄνδρʼ ἐφίλησεν,
καὶ τοὺς ἀργυρέους οὔ ποτʼ ἀποστρέφεται.
Νέστωρ ἡ Παφίη. δοκέω δʼ ὅτι καὶ Δανάῃ Ζεὺς
οὐ χρυσός, χρυσοῦς δʼ ἦλθε φέρων ἑκατόν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.109: δραχμῆς Εὐρώπην τὴν Ἀτθίδα, μήτε
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
δραχμῆς Εὐρώπην τὴν Ἀτθίδα, μήτε φοβηθεὶς
μηδένα, μήτʼ ἄλλως ἀντιλέγουσαν, ἔχε,
καὶ στρωμνὴν παρέχουσαν ἀμεμφέα, χὠπότε χειμών,
ἄνθρακας. ἦ ῥα μάτην, Ζεῦ φίλε, βοῦς ἐγένου.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.198: ὥριον ἀνθήσαντας ὑπὸ κροτάφοισιν ἰούλους
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ὥριον ἀνθήσαντας ὑπὸ κροτάφοισιν ἰούλους
κειράμενος, γενύων ἄρσενας ἀγλαΐας,
Φοίβῳ θῆκε Λύκῶν, πρῶτον γέρας· εὔξατο δʼ οὕτως
καὶ πολιὴν λευκῶν κεῖραι ἀπὸ κροτάφων.
τοίην ἀλλʼ ἐπίνευε, τίθει δέ μιν, ὡς πρό γε τοῖον,
ὣς αὖτις πολιῷ γήραϊ νιφόμενον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.18: ἀνέρα μὴ πέτρῃ τεκμαίρεο. λιτὸς
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἀνέρα μὴ πέτρῃ τεκμαίρεο. λιτὸς ὁ τύμβος
ὀφθῆναι, μεγάλου δʼ ὀστέα φωτὸς ἔχει.
εἰδήσεις Ἀλκμᾶνα, λύρης ἐλατῆρα Λακαίνης
ἔξοχον, ὃν Μουσέων ἐννέʼ ἀριθμὸς ἔχει·
κεῖται δʼ ἠπείροις διδύμοις ἔρις, εἴθʼ ὅγε Λυδὸς,
εἴτε Λάκων πολλαὶ μητέρες ὑμνοπόλων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.39: ὁ τραγικὸν φώνημα καὶ ὀφρυόεσσαν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ὁ τραγικὸν φώνημα καὶ ὀφρυόεσσαν ἀοιδὴν
πυργώσας στιβαρῇ πρῶτος ἐν εὐεπίῃ,
Αἰσχύλος Εὐφορίωνος, Ἐλευσινίης ἑκὰς αἴης
κεῖται, κυδαίνων σήματι Τρινακρίην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.168: εὐχέσθω τις ἔπειτα γυνὴ τόκον
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
εὐχέσθω τις ἔπειτα γυνὴ τόκον, εἶπε Πολυξώ,
γαστέρʼ ὑπὸ τρισσῶν ῥηγνυμένη τεκέων
μαίης δʼ ἐν παλάμῃσι χύθη νέκυς· οἱ δʼ ἐπὶ γαῖαν
ὤλισθον κοίλων ἄρρενες ἐκ λαγόνων,
μητέρος ἐκ νεκρῆς ζωὸς γόνος· εἷς ἄρα δαίμων
τῆς μὲν ἀπὸ ζωὴν εἵλετο, τοῖς δʼ ἔπορεν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.185: Αὐσονίη με Λίβυσσαν ἔχει κόνις
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Αὐσονίη με Λίβυσσαν ἔχει κόνις, ἄγχι δὲ Ῥώμης
κεῖμαι παρθενικὴ τῇδε παρὰ ψαμάθῳ·
ἡ δέ με θρεψαμένη Πομπηίη ἀντὶ θυγατρός,
κλαυσαμένη τύμβῳ θῆκεν ἐλευθερίῳ,
πῦρ ἕτερον σπεύδουσα· τὸ δʼ ἔφθασεν, οὐδὲ κατʼ εὐχὴν
ἡμετέραν ἧψεν λαμπάδα Περσεφόνη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.216: κύματα καὶ τρηχύς με κλύδων
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
κύματα καὶ τρηχύς με κλύδων ἐπὶ χέρσον ἔσυρεν
δελφῖνα, ξείνοις κοινὸν ὅραμα τύχης.
ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ μὲν γαίης ἐλέῳ τόπος· οἱ γὰρ ἰδόντες
εὐθύ με πρὸς τύμβους ἔστεφον εὐσεβέες·
νῦν δὲ τεκοῦσα θάλασσα διώλεσε. τίς παρὰ πόντῳ
πίστις, ὃς οὐδʼ ἰδίης φείσατο συντροφίης;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.236: οὐχὶ Θεμιστοκλέους Μάγνης τάφος· ἀλλὰ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
οὐχὶ Θεμιστοκλέους Μάγνης τάφος· ἀλλὰ κέχωσμαι
Ἑλλήνων φθονερῆς σῆμα κακοκρισίης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.286: δύσμορε Νικάνωρ, πολιῷ μεμαραμμένε πόντῳ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
δύσμορε Νικάνωρ, πολιῷ μεμαραμμένε πόντῳ,
κεῖσαι δὴ ξείνῃ γυμνὸς ἐπʼ ἠιόνι,
ἢ σύ γε πρὸς πέτρῃσι· τὰ δʼ ὄλβια κεῖνα μέλαθρα
φροῦδα 〈καὶ ἡ〉 πάσης ἐλπὶς ὄλωλε Τύρου.
οὐδὲ τί σε κτεάνων ἐρρύσατο· φεῦ, ἐλεεινέ,
ὤλεο μοχθήσας ἰχθύσι καὶ πελάγει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.287: καὶ νέκυν ἀπρήυντος ἀνιήσει με
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
καὶ νέκυν ἀπρήυντος ἀνιήσει με θάλασσα
Λῦσιν, ἐρημαίῃ κρυπτὸν ὑπὸ σπιλάδι,
στρηνὲς ἀεὶ φωνεῦσα παρʼ οὔατι, καὶ παρὰ κωφὸν
σῆμα. τί μʼ, ὤνθρωποι, τῇδε παρῳκίσατε,
ἣ πνοιῆς χήρωσε τὸν οὐκ ἐπὶ φορτίδι νηὶ
ἔμπορον, ἀλλʼ ὀλίγης ναυτίλον εἰρεσίης
θηκαμένη ναυηγόν; ὁ δʼ ἐκ πόντοιο ματεύων
ζωήν, ἐκ πόντου καὶ μόρον εἱλκυσάμην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.288: οὐδετέρης ὅλος εἰμὶ θανὼν νέκυς
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
οὐδετέρης ὅλος εἰμὶ θανὼν νέκυς, ἀλλὰ θάλασσα
καὶ χθὼν τὴν ἀπʼ ἐμεῦ μοῖραν ἔχουσιν ἴσην.
σάρκα γὰρ ἐν πόντῳ φάγον ἰχθύες· ὀστέα δʼ αὖτε
βέβρασται ψυχρῇ τῇδε παρʼ ἠιόνι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.289: ἀνθέα τὸν ναυηγὸν ἐπὶ στόμα
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἀνθέα τὸν ναυηγὸν ἐπὶ στόμα Πηνειοῖο
νυκτὸς ὑπὲρ βαιῆς νηξάμενον σανίδος,
μούνιος ἐκ θάμνοιο θορὼν λύκος, ἄσκοπον ἄνδρα,
ἔκτανεν. ὦ γαίης κύματα πιστότερα,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.367: Αὔσονος Ἠγερίου με λέγειν νέκυν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Αὔσονος Ἠγερίου με λέγειν νέκυν, ᾧ μετιόντι
νύμφην ὀφθαλμοὺς ἀμβλὺ κατέσχε νέφος,
ὄμμασι δὲ πνοιὴν συναπέσβεσε μοῦνον ἰδόντος
κούρην. φεῦ κείνης, Ἥλιε, θευμορίης·
ἔρροι δὴ κεῖνο φθονερὸν σέλας, εἴθʼ Ὑμέναιος
ἧψέ μιν οὐκ ἐθέλων, εἴτʼ Ἀίδης ἐθέλων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.369: Ἀντιπάτρου ῥητῆρος ἐγὼ τάφος· ἡλίκα
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Ἀντιπάτρου ῥητῆρος ἐγὼ τάφος· ἡλίκα δʼ ἔπνει
ἔργα, Πανελλήνων πεύθεο μαρτυρίης.
κεῖται δʼ ἀμφήριστος, Ἀθηνόθεν, εἴτʼ ἀπὸ Νείλου
ἦν γένος· ἠπείρων δʼ ἄξιος ἀμφοτέρων.
ἄστεα καὶ δʼ ἄλλως ἑνὸς αἵματος, ὡς λόγος Ἕλλην
κλήρῳ δʼ ἡ μὲν ἀεὶ Παλλάδος, ἡ δὲ Διός.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.390: Κυλλήνην ὄρος Ἀρκάδων ἀκούεις
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Κυλλήνην ὄρος Ἀρκάδων ἀκούεις·
αὕτη σῆμʼ ἐπίκειτʼ Ἀπολλοδώρῳ.
Πίσηθέν μιν ἰόντα νυκτὸς ὥρῃ
ἔκτεινεν Διόθεν πεσὼν κεραυνός.
τηλοῦ δʼ Αἰανέης τε καὶ Βεροίης
νικηθεὶς Διὸς ὁ δρομεὺς καθεύδει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.398: οὐκ οἶδʼ εἰ Διόνυσον ὀνόσσομαι
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
οὐκ οἶδʼ εἰ Διόνυσον ὀνόσσομαι, ἢ Διὸς ὄμβρον
μέμψομʼ ὀλισθηροὶ δʼ εἰς πόδας ἀμφότεροι.
ἀγρόθε γὰρ κατιόντα Πολύξενον ἔκ ποτε δαιτὸς
τύμβος ἔχει γλίσχρων ἐξεριπόντα λόφων
κεῖται δʼ Αἰολίδος Σμύρνης ἑκάς. ἀλλά τις ὄρφνης
δειμαίνοι μεθύων ἀτραπὸν ὑετίην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.402: χειμερίου νιφετοῖο περὶ θριγκοῖσι τακέντος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
χειμερίου νιφετοῖο περὶ θριγκοῖσι τακέντος
δῶμα πεσὸν τὴν γραῦν ἔκτανε Λυσιδίκην
σῆμα δέ οἱ κωμῆται ὁμώλακες οὐκ ἀπʼ ὀρυκτῆς
γαίης, ἀλλʼ αὐτὸν πύργον ἔθεντο τάφον,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.530: μούναν σὺν τέκνοις νεκυοστόλε δέξο
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
μούναν σὺν τέκνοις νεκυοστόλε δέξο με πορθμεῦ
τὰν λάλον ἀρκεῖ σοι φόρτος ὁ Τανταλίδης·
πληρώσει γαστὴρ μία σὸν σκάφος· εἴσιδε κούρους
καὶ κούρας, Φοίβου σκῦλα καὶ Ἀρτέμιδος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.531: αὐτά τοι, τρέσσαντι παρὰ χρέος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
αὐτά τοι, τρέσσαντι παρὰ χρέος, ὤπασεν ᾅδαν,
βαψαμένα κοίλων ἐντὸς ἄρη λαγόνων,
μάτηρ ἅ σ’ ἔτεκεν, Δαμάτριε· φᾶ δὲ σίδαρον
παιδὸς ἑοῦ φύρδαν μεστὸν ἔχουσα φόνου,
ἀφριόεν κοναβηδὸν ἐπιπρίουσα γένειον,
δερκομένα λοξαῖς, οἷα Λάκαινα, κόραις
“ λεῖπε τὸν Εὐρώταν, ἴθι Τάρταρον· ἁνίκα δειλὰν
οἶσθα φυγάν, τελέθεις οὔτʼ ἐμὸς οὔτε Λάκων.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.629: ἦ χθαμαλὴν ὑπέδυς ὁ τόσος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἦ χθαμαλὴν ὑπέδυς ὁ τόσος κόνιν; εἰς σέ τις ἀθρῶν,
Σώκρατες, Ἑλλήνων μέμψεται ἀκρισίην·
νηλέες, οἳ τὸν ἄριστον ἀπώλεσαν, οὐδὲ ἓν αἰδοῖ
δόντες. τοιοῦτοι πολλάκι Κεκροπίδαι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.637: Πύρρος ὁ μουνερέτης ὀλίγῃ νηῒ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Πύρρος ὁ μουνερέτης ὀλίγῃ νηῒ λεπτὰ ματεύων
φυκία καὶ τριχίνης μαινίδας ἐκ καθέτης,
ἠιόνων ἀποτῆλε τυπεὶς κατέδουπε κεραυνῷ·
νηῦς δὲ πρὸς αἰγιαλοὺς ἔδραμεν αὐτομάτη
ἀγγελίην θείῳ καὶ λιγνύϊ μηνύουσα,
καὶ φράσαι Ἀργῴην οὐκ ἐπόθησε τρόπιν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.639: πᾶσα θάλασσα θάλασσα· τί Κυκλάδας
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.640: ῥιγηλὴ ναύταις ἐρίφων δύσις, ἀλλὰ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ῥιγηλὴ ναύταις ἐρίφων δύσις, ἀλλὰ Πύρωνι
πουλὺ γαληναίη χείματος ἐχθροτέρη·
νῆα γὰρ ἀπνοΐῃ πεπεδημένου ἔφθασε ναύταις
ληιστέων ταχινὴ δίκροτος ἐσσυμένη·
χεῖμα δέ μιν προφυγόντα γαληναίῳ ἐπʼ ὀλέθρῳ
ἔκτανον ἆ λυγρῆς δειλὲ καχορμισίης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.666: οὗτος ὁ Λειάνδροιο διάπλοος, οὗτος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
οὗτος ὁ Λειάνδροιο διάπλοος, οὗτος ὁ πόντου
πορθμὸς, ὁ μὴ μούνῳ τῷ φιλέοντι βαρύς·
ταῦθʼ Ἡροῦς τὰ πάροιθεν ἐπαύλια, τοῦτο τὸ πύργου;
λείψανον, ὁ προδότης ὧδʼ ἐπέκειτο λύχνος.
κοινὸς δʼ ἀμφοτέρους ὅδʼ ἔχει τάφος, εἰσέτι καὶ νῦν
κείνῳ τῷ φθονερῷ μεμφομένους ἀνέμῳ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.705: Στρυμόνι καὶ μεγάλῳ πεποτισμένον Ἑλλησπόντῳ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Στρυμόνι καὶ μεγάλῳ πεποτισμένον Ἑλλησπόντῳ
ἠρίον Ἠδωνῆς Φυλλίδος, Ἀμφίπολι,
λοιπά τοι Αἰθοπίης Βραυρωνίδος ἴχνια νηοῦ
μίμνει, καὶ ποταμοῦ τἀμφιμάχητον ὕδωρ,
τὴν δὲ ποτʼ Αἰγείδαις μεγάλην ἔριν ὡς ἁλιανθὲς
τρῦχος ἐπʼ ἀμφοτέραις δερκόμεθʼ ἠιόσιν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.3: εἰνοδίην καρύην με παρερχομένοις ἐφύτευσαν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
εἰνοδίην καρύην με παρερχομένοις ἐφύτευσαν
παισὶ λιθοβλήτου παίγνιον εὐστοχίης.
πάντας δʼ ἀκρεμόνας τε καὶ εὐθαλέας ὀροδάμνους
κέκλασμαι, πυκιναῖς χερμάσι βαλλομένη.
δένδρεσιν εὐκάρποις οὐδὲν πλέον ἦ γὰρ ἔγωγε
δυσδαίμων ἐς ἐμὴν ὕβριν ἐκαρποφόρουν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.10: Πούλυπος εἰναλίῃ ποτʼ ἐπὶ προβλῆτι
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Πούλυπος εἰναλίῃ ποτʼ ἐπὶ προβλῆτι τανυσθεὶς
ἠελίῳ ψύχειν πολλὸν ἀνῆκε πέδα·
οὔπω δʼ ἦν πέτρῃ ἴκελος χρόα, τοὔνεκα καί μιν
αἰετὸς ἐκ νεφέων ὀξὺς ἔμαρψεν ἰδών
πλοχμοῖς δʼ εἰλιχθεὶς πέσεν εἰς ἅλα δύσμορος· ἦ ῥα
ἄμφω καὶ θήρης ἤμβροτε καὶ βιότου.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.26: τάσδε θεογλώσσους Ἑλικὼν ἔθρεψε γυναῖκας
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
τάσδε θεογλώσσους Ἑλικὼν ἔθρεψε γυναῖκας
ὕμνοις, καὶ Μακεδὼν Πιερίας σκόπελος,
Πρήξιλλαν, Μοιρώ, Ἀνύτης στόμα, θῆλυν Ὅμηρον,
Λεσβιάδων Σαπφὼ κόσμον ἐυπλοκάμων,
Ἤρινναν, Τελέσιλλαν ἀγακλέα, καὶ σέ, Κόριννα,
θοῦριν Ἀθηναίης ἀσπίδα μελψαμέναν,
Νοσσίδα θηλύγλωσσον, ἰδὲ γλυκυαχέα Μύρτιν,
πάσας ἀενάων ἐργάτιδας σελίδων.
ἐννέα μὲν Μούσας μέγας Οὐρανός, ἐννέα δʼ αὐτὰς
γαῖα τέκεν, θνατοῖς ἄφθιτον εὐφροσύναν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.46: πηρὸς ἄπαις, ἢ φέγγος ἰδεῖν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
πηρὸς ἄπαις, ἢ φέγγος ἰδεῖν ἢ παῖδα τεκέσθαι
εὐξαμένη, δοιῆς ἔμμορεν εὐτυχίης·
τίκτε γὰρ εὐθὺς ἄελπτα μετʼ οὐ πολύ, καὶ τριποθήτου
αὐτῆμαρ γλυκερὸν φέγγος ἐσεῖδε φάους.
Ἄρτεμις ἀμφοτέροισιν ἐπήκοος, ἥ τε λοχείης
μαῖα, καὶ ἀργεννῶν φωσφόρος ἡ σελάων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.59: τέσσαρες αἰωροῦσι τανυπτερύγων ἐπὶ νώτων
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
τέσσαρες αἰωροῦσι τανυπτερύγων ἐπὶ νώτων
νῖκαι ἰσηρίθμους υἱέας ἀθανάτων
ἁ μὲν Ἀθηναίαν πολεμαδόκον, ἁ δʼ Ἀφροδίταν,
ἁ δὲ τὸν Ἀλκείδαν, ἁ δʼ ἀφόβητον Ἄρη,
σεῖο κατʼ εὐόροφον γραπτὸν τέγος· ἐς δὲ νέονται
οὐρανόν, ὦ Ῥώμας Γαῖε πάτρας ἔρυμα.
θείη ἀνίκατον μὲν ὁ βουφάγος. ἁ δέ σε Κύπρις
εὔγαμον, εὔμητιν Παλλάς, ἄτρεστον Ἄρης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.72: εὔκολος Ἑρμείας, ὦ ποιμένες, ἐν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
εὔκολος Ἑρμείας, ὦ ποιμένες, ἐν δὲ γάλακτι
χαίρων καὶ δρυΐνῳ σπενδομένοις μέλιτι·
ἀλλʼ οὐχ Ἡρακλέης· ἕνα δὲ κτίλον ἢ παχὺν ἄρνα
αἰτεῖ, καὶ πάντως ἓν θύος ἐκλέγεται.
ἀλλὰ λύκους εἴργει. τί δὲ τὸ πλέον, εἰ τὸ φυλαχθὲν
ὄλλυται εἴτε λύκοις, εἴθʼ ὑπὸ τοῦ φύλακος;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.77: Πριομένα κάλλει Γανυμήδεος εἶπέ ποθʼ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Πριομένα κάλλει Γανυμήδεος εἶπέ ποθʼ Ἥρα,
θυμοβόρον ζάλου κέντρον ἔχουσα νόῳ
“ ἄρσεν πῦρ ἔτεκεν Τροία Διί· τοιγὰρ ἐγὼ πῦρ
πέμψω ἐπὶ Τροίᾳ, πῆμα φέροντα Πάριν·
ἥξει δʼ Ἰλιάδαις οὐκ ἀετός, ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ θοίναν
γῦπες, ὅταν Δαναοὶ σκῦλα φέρωσι πόνων.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.82: Μηδʼ ὅτʼ ἐπʼ ἀγκύρης, ὀλοῇ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Μηδʼ ὅτʼ ἐπʼ ἀγκύρης, ὀλοῇ πίστευε θαλάσσῃ,
ναυτίλε, μηδʼ εἴ τοι πείσματα χέρσος ἔχοι.
καὶ γὰρ Ἴων ὅρμῳ ἔνι κάππεσεν ἐς δὲ κόλυμβον
ναύτου τὰς ταχινὰς οἶνος ἔδησε χέρας.
φεῦγε χοροιτυπίην ἐπινήιον ἐχθρὸς Ἰάκχῳ
πόντος· Τυρσηνοὶ τοῦτον ἔθεντο νόμον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.92: ἀρκεῖ τέττιγας μεθύσαι δρόσος· ἀλλὰ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἀρκεῖ τέττιγας μεθύσαι δρόσος· ἀλλὰ πιόντες
ἀείδειν κύκνων εἰσὶ γεγωνότεροι.
ὣς καὶ ἀοιδὸς ἀνήρ, ξενίων χάριν, ἀνταποδοῦναι
ὕμνους εὐέρκταις οἶδε, παθὼν ὀλίγα.
τοὔνεκά σοι πρώτως μὲν ἀμείβομαι· ἢν δʼ ἐθέλωσιν
Μοῖραι, πολλάκι μοι κείσεαι ἐν σελίσιν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.93: Ἀντίπατρος Πείσωνι γενέθλιον ὤπασε βίβλον
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Ἀντίπατρος Πείσωνι γενέθλιον ὤπασε βίβλον
μικρήν, ἐν δὲ μιῇ νυκτὶ πονησάμενος.
ἵλαος ἀλλὰ δέχοιτο, καὶ αἰνήσειεν ἀοιδόν,
Ζεὺς μέγας ὡς ὀλίγῳ πειθόμενος λιβάνῳ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.96: Ἀντιγένης ὁ Γελῷος ἔπος ποτὲ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Ἀντιγένης ὁ Γελῷος ἔπος ποτὲ τοῦτο θυγατρὶ
εἶπεν, ὅτʼ ἦν ἤδη νεύμενος εἰς Ἀίδην
“ παρθένε καλλιπάρῃε, κόρη δʼ ἐμή, ἴσχε συνεργὸν
ἠλακάτην, ἀρκεῦν κτῆμα πένητι βίῳ·
ἢν δʼ ἵκᾐ εἰς ὑμέναιον, Ἀχαιίδος ἤθεα μητρὸς
χρηστὰ φύλασσε, πόσει προῖκα βεβαιοτάτην.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.112: τρὶς δέκα με πνεύσειν καὶ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
τρὶς δέκα με πνεύσειν καὶ δὶς τρία μάντιες ἄστρων
φασὶν ἐμοὶ δʼ ἀρκεῖ καὶ δεκὰς ἡ τριτάτη·
τοῦτο γὰρ ἀνθρώποις βιοτῆς ὅρος· ἡ δʼ ἐπὶ τούτοις
Νέστορι· καὶ Νέστωρ δʼ ἤλυθεν εἰς ἀίδην,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.149: εἶχεν Ἀριστείδης ὁ βοκέρριος οὐκ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
εἶχεν Ἀριστείδης ὁ βοκέρριος οὐκ ἀπὸ πολλῶν
πολλά, μιῆς δʼ ὄιος καὶ βοὸς εὐπορίην.
ἀλλὰ γὰρ οὐδʼ ὁ πένης ἔφυγε φθόνον ἤματι δʼ αὐτῷ
θῆρες ὄιν, τὴν βοῦν δʼ ὤλεσε δυστοκίη.
μισήσας δʼ ἀβληχὲς ἐπαύλιον, ἅμματι πήρης
ἐκ ταύτης βιοτὴν ἀχράδος ἐκρέμασεν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.186: βίβλοι Ἀριστοφάνευς, θεῖος πόνος, αἷσιν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
βίβλοι Ἀριστοφάνευς, θεῖος πόνος, αἷσιν Ἀχαρνεὺς
κισσὸς ἐπὶ χλοερὴν πουλὺς ἔσεισε κόμην.
ἠνίδʼ ὅσον Διόνυσον ἔχει σελίς, οἷα δὲ μῦθοι
ἠχεῦσιν, φοβερῶν πληθόμενοι χαρίτων.
ὦ καὶ θυμὸν ἄριστε, καὶ Ἑλλάδος ἤθεσιν ἶσα,
κωμικέ, καὶ στύξας ἄξια καὶ γελάσας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.215: αἰεὶ θηλυτέρῃσιν ὕδωρ κακὸν Ἑλλήσποντος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
αἰεὶ θηλυτέρῃσιν ὕδωρ κακὸν Ἑλλήσποντος,
ξεῖνε· Κλεονίκης πεύθεο Δυρραχίδος.
πλῶε γὰρ ἐς Σηστὸν μετὰ νυμφίον ἐν δὲ μελαίνῃ
φορτίδι τὴν Ἕλλης μοῖραν ἀπεπλάσατο.
Ἡροῖ δειλαίη, σὺ μὲν ἀνέρα,, Δηίμαχος δὲ
νύμφην, ἐν παύροις ὠλέσατε σταδίοις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.231: αὔην με πλατάνιστον ἐφερπύζουσα καλύπτει
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
αὔην με πλατάνιστον ἐφερπύζουσα καλύπτει
ἄμπελος· ὀθνείῃ δʼ ἀμφιτέθηλα κόμῃ,
ἡ πρὶν ἐμοῖς θαλέθουσιν ἐνιθρέψασ’ ὀροδάμνοις
βότρυας, ἡ ταύτης οὐκ ἀπετηλοτέρη·
τοίην μέντοι ἔπειτα τιθηνείσθω τις ἑταίρην,
ἥτις ἀμείψασθαι καὶ νέκυν οἶδε μόνη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.238: βούπαις ὡπόλλων τόδε χάλκεον ἔργον
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
βούπαις ὡπόλλων τόδε χάλκεον ἔργον Ὀνατᾶ,
ἀγλαΐης Λητοῖ καὶ Διὶ μαρτυρίη,
οὔθʼ ὅτι τῆσδε μάτην Ζεὺς ἤρατο, χὤτι κατʼ αἶνον
ὄμματα καὶ κεφαλὴν ἀγλαὸς ὁ Κρονίδης.
οὐδʼ Ἥρῃ νεμεσητὸν ἐχεύατο χαλκὸν Ὀνατᾶς,
ὃν μετʼ Ἐλειθυίης τοῖον ἀπεπλάσατο.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.241: βουκόλος ἔπλεο, Φοῖβε, Ποσειδάων δὲ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
βουκόλος ἔπλεο, Φοῖβε, Ποσειδάων δὲ καβάλλης,
κύκνος Ζεύς, Ἄμμων δʼ ὡμφιβόητος ὄφις,
χοἰ μὲν ἐπʼ ἠιθέας, σὺ δὲ παιδικός, ὄφρα λάθοιτε·
ἐστὲ γὰρ οὐ πειθοῦς εὐνέται, ἀλλὰ βίης.
Εὐαγόρας δʼ ὢν χαλκὸς ἄτερ δόλου αὐτὸς ἐναργὴς
πάντας καὶ πάσας, οὐ μεταβαλλόμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.266: ἵμερον αὐλήσαντι πολυτρήτων διὰ λωτῶν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἵμερον αὐλήσαντι πολυτρήτων διὰ λωτῶν
εἶπε λιγυφθόγγῳ Φοῖβος ἐπὶ Γλαφύρῳ·
“ Μαρσύη, ἐψεύσω τεὸν εὕρεμα, τοὺς γὰρ Ἀθήνης
αὐλοὺς ἐκ Φρυγίης οὗτος ἐληΐσατο·
εἰ δὲ σὺ τοιούτοις τότʼ ἐνέπνεες, οὐκ ἂν Ὕαγνις
τὴν ἐπὶ Μαιάνδρῳ κλαῦσε δύσαυλον ἔριν.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.268: Κρῆσσα κύων ἐλάφοιο κατʼ ἴχνιον
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Κρῆσσα κύων ἐλάφοιο κατʼ ἴχνιον ἔδραμε Γοργώ,
ἔγκυος, ἀμφοτέρην Ἄρτεμιν εὐξαμένη·
τίκτε δʼ ἀποκτείνουσα· θοὴ δʼ ἐπένευσεν Ἐλευθὼ
ἄμφω, εὐαγρίης δῶρα καὶ εὐτοκίης·
καὶ νῦν ἐννέα παισὶ διδοῖ γάλα. φεύγετε, Κρῆσσαι
κεμμάδες, ἐκ τοκάδων τέκνα διδασκόμεναι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.269: Κλασθείσης ποτὲ νηὸς ἐν ὕδατι
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Κλασθείσης ποτὲ νηὸς ἐν ὕδατι δῆριν ἔθεντο
δισσοὶ ὑπὲρ μούνης μαρνάμενοι σανίδος.
τύψε μὲν Ἀνταγόρης Πεισίστρατον οὐ νεμεσητόν,
ἦν γὰρ ὑπὲρ ψυχῆς· ἀλλʼ ἐμέλησε Δίκῃ.
νῆχε δʼ ὁ μὲν, τὸν δʼ εἷλε κύων ἁλός. ἦ παναλάστωρ
κηρῶν οὐδʼ ὑγρῷ παύεται ἐν πελάγει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.282: ξεῖνοι, παρθένος εἰμὶ τὸ δένδρεον
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ξεῖνοι, παρθένος εἰμὶ τὸ δένδρεον εἴπατε δάφνης
φείσασθαι δμώων χερσὶν ἑτοιμοτόμοις·
ἀντὶ δʼ ἐμεῦ κομάρου τις ὁδοιπόρος ἢ τερεβίνθου
δρεπτέσθω χθαμαλὴν ἐς χύσιν οὐ γὰρ ἑκάς·
ἀλλʼ ἀπʼ ἐμεῦ ποταμὸς μὲν ὅσον τρία, τοῦ δʼ ἀπὸ πηγῶν
ὕλη πανθηλὴς δοιὰ πέλεθρʼ ἀπέχει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.297: Στέλλευ ἐπʼ Εὐφρήτην, Ζηνὸς τέκος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Στέλλευ ἐπʼ Εὐφρήτην, Ζηνὸς τέκος· εἰς σὲ γὰρ ἤδη
ἠῷοι Πάρθων αὐτομολοῦσι πόδες.
στέλλευ, ἄναξ· δήεις δὲ φόβῳ κεχαλασμένα τόξα,
Καῖσαρ· πατρῴων δʼ ἄρξαι ἀπʼ ἐντολέων
Ῥώμην δʼ, ὠκεανῷ περιτέρμονα πάντοθεν, αὐτὸς
πρῶτος ἀνερχομένῳ σφράγισαι ἠελίῳ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.302: τὸ βρέφος Ἑρμώνακτα διεχρήσασθε μέλισσαι
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
τὸ βρέφος Ἑρμώνακτα διεχρήσασθε μέλισσαι
ʽφ̔εῦ κύνεσ̓ ἑρπυστήν, κηρία μαιόμενον
πολλάκι δʼ ἐξ ὑμέων ἐψισμένον ὠλέσατʼ, αἰαῖ,
κέντροις. εἰ δʼ ὀφίων φωλεὰ μεμφόμεθα,
πείθεο Λυσιδίκῃ καὶ Ἀμύντορι μηδὲ μελίσσας
αἰνεῖν κἀκείναις πικρὸν ἔνεστι μέλι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.305: ὕδατος ἀκρήτου κεκορημένῳ ἄγχι παραστὰς
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ὕδατος ἀκρήτου κεκορημένῳ ἄγχι παραστὰς
χθιζὸν ἐμοὶ λεχέων Βάκχος ἔλεξε τάδε·
“ εὕδεις ἄξιον ὕπνον ἀπεχθομένων Ἀφροδίτῃ·
εἰπέ μοι, ὦ νήφων, πεύθεαι Ἱππολύτου;
τάρβει, μή τι πάθῃς ἐναλίγκιον.” ὣς ὁ μὲν εἰπὼν
ᾤχετʼ ἐμοὶ δʼ ἀπὸ τῆς οὐκέτι τερπνὸν ὕδωρ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.309: χειμέριον καίουσαν ἐφʼ ἑστίῃ ἄνθρακα
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
χειμέριον καίουσαν ἐφʼ ἑστίῃ ἄνθρακα Γοργὼ
τὴν γρηῢν βροντῆς ἐξεπάταξε φόβος·
πνεύμονα δὲ ψυχθεῖσα κατήμυσεν. ἦν ἄρα μέσσῃ
γήρως καὶ θανάτου λειπομένη πρόφασις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.407: Δμώιον Ἱπποκράτευς ἔθανε βρέφος, ἐς
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Δμώιον Ἱπποκράτευς ἔθανε βρέφος, ἐς πλατὺ πόντου
χεῖλος γειτοσύνης ἑρπύσαν ἐκ καλύβης,
πλεῖον ἐπεὶ μαζῶν ἔπιεν ποτόν. ἔρρε θάλασσα
ἣ βρέφος ὡς μήτηρ ψεύσαο δεξαμένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.417: θηρευτὴν Λάμπωνα Μίδου κύνα δίψα
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
θηρευτὴν Λάμπωνα Μίδου κύνα δίψα κατέκτα,
καίπερ ὑπὲρ ψυχῆς πολλὰ πονησάμενον.
ποσσὶ γὰρ ὤρυσσεν νοτερὸν πέδον, ἀλλὰ τὸ νωθὲς
πίδακος ἐκ τυφλῆς οὐκ ἐτάχυνεν ὕδωρ·
πῖπτε δʼ ἀπαυδήσας· ἡ δʼ ἔβλυσεν. ἦ ἄρα, Νύμφαι,
Λάμπωνι κταμένων μῆνιν ἔθεσθʼ ἐλάφων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.418: ἴσχετε χεῖρα μυλαῖον, ἀλετρίδες· εὕδετε
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἴσχετε χεῖρα μυλαῖον, ἀλετρίδες· εὕδετε μακρά,
κἢν ὄρθρον προλέγῃ γῆρυς ἀλεκτρυόνων·
Δηὼ γὰρ Νύμφαισι χερῶν ἐπετείλατο μόχθους·
αἱ δὲ κατʼ ἀκροτάτην ἁλλόμεναι τροχιήν,
ἄξονα δινεύουσιν ὁ δʼ ἀκτίνεσσιν ἑλικταῖς
στρωφᾷ Νισυρίων κοῖλα βάρη μυλάκων.
γευόμεθʼ ἀρχαίου βιότου πάλιν, εἰ δίχα μόχθου
δαίνυσθαι Δηοῦς ἔργα διδασκόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.420: μὴ κλαίων τὸν Ἔρωτα δόκει
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
μὴ κλαίων τὸν Ἔρωτα δόκει, Τηλέμβροτε, πείσειν,
μηδʼ ὀλίγῳ παύσειν ὕδατι πῦρ ἀτενές.
χρυσὸς Ἔρωτος ἀεὶ παιώνιος· ἐσβέσθη δὲ
οὐδὲ τότʼ ἐν πολλῷ τικτόμενος πελάγει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.421: νῆσοι ἐρημαῖαι, τρύφεα χθονός, ἃς
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
νῆσοι ἐρημαῖαι, τρύφεα χθονός, ἃς κελαδεινὸς
ζωστὴρ Αἰγαίου κύματος ἐντὸς ἔχει,
Σίφνον ἐμιμήσασθε καὶ αὐχμηρὴν Φολέγανδρον,
τλήμονες, ἀρχαίην δʼ ὠλέσατʼ ἀγλαΐην.
ἦ ῥʼ ὑμᾶς ἐδίδαξεν ἕνα τρόπον ἥ ποτε λευκὴ
δῆλος, ἐρημαίου δαίμονος ἀρξαμένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.428: σοί με, Θρηϊκίης σκυληφόρε, Θεσσαλονίκη
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
σοί με, Θρηϊκίης σκυληφόρε, Θεσσαλονίκη
μήτηρ ἡ πάσης πέμψε Μακηδονίης.
ἀείδω δʼ ὑπὸ σοὶ δεδμημένον Ἄρεα Βεσσῶν,
ὅσσ’ ἐδάην πολέμου πάντʼ ἀναλεξάμενος.
ἀλλά μοι ὡς θεὸς ἔσσο κατήκοος, εὐχομένου δὲ
κλῦθι. τίς ἐς Μούσας οὔατος ἀσχολίη;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.517: Ὀρφεὺς θῆρας ἔπειθε, σὺ δʼ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Ὀρφεὺς θῆρας ἔπειθε, σὺ δʼ Ὀρφέα· Φοῖβος ἐνίκα
τὸν Φρύγα, σοὶ δʼ εἴκει μελπομένῳ, Γλάφυρε,
οὔνομα καὶ τέχνης καὶ σώματος. οὔ κεν Ἀθήνη
ἔρριψεν λωτοὺς τοῖα μελιζομένη,
οἷα σὺ ποικιλοτερπές· ἀφυπνώσαι κεν ἀκούων
αὐτὸς Πασιθέης Ὕπνος ἐν ἀγκαλίσιν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.541: Θειογένης Πείσωνι τὰ τεχνήεντα κύπελλα
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Θειογένης Πείσωνι τὰ τεχνήεντα κύπελλα
πέμπει· χωροῦμεν δʼ οὐρανὸν ἀμφότερα·
δοιὰ γὰρ ἐκ σφαίρης τετμήμεθα, καὶ τὸ μὲν ἡμῶν
τοὺς νοτίους, τὸ δʼ ἔχει τείρεα τἀν Βορέῃ.
ἀλλὰ σὺ μηκέτʼ Ἄρητον ἐπίβλεπε· δισσὰ γὰρ ἀμφοῖν
μέτρα πιὼν ἀθρεῖς πάντα τὰ φαινόμενα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.550: κλεινὴν οὐκ ἀπόφημι· σὲ γὰρ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
κλεινὴν οὐκ ἀπόφημι· σὲ γὰρ προπάροιθεν ἔθηκαν
κλῄζεσθαι πτηνοί, Τῆνε, Βορηιάδαι.
ἀλλὰ καὶ Ὀρτυγίην εἶχε κλέος, οὔνομα δʼ αὐτῆς
ἤρχετο Ῥιπαίων ἄχρις Ὑπερβορέων.
νῦν δὲ σὺ μὲν ζώεις, ἡ δʼ οὐκέτι· τίς κεν ἐώλπει
ὄψεσθαι Τήνου Δῆλον ἐρημοτέρην;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.552: καὶ Μακεδὼν ὁ σίδηρος ἐν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
καὶ Μακεδὼν ὁ σίδηρος ἐν ἄορι, καὶ τὰ πρὸς ἀλκὴν
τῆς ἀπʼ Ἀλεξάνδρου χειρὸς ἐπιστάμενος,
Πείσων, σὴν ποθέων ἱκόμην χέρα· τοῦτο δὲ φωνῶ·
χαίρων δεξιτερὴν εὗρον ὀφειλομένην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.557: ὁ σταδιεὺς Ἀρίης ὁ Μενεκλέος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ὁ σταδιεὺς Ἀρίης ὁ Μενεκλέος οὐ κατελέγχει
Περσέα, σὸν κτίστην, Ταρσὲ Κίλισσα πόλι.
τοῖοι γὰρ παιδὸς πτηνοὶ πόδες· οὐδʼ ἂν ἐκείνῳ
οὐδʼ αὐτὸς Περσεὺς νῶτον ἔδειξε θέων.
ἢ γὰρ ἐφʼ ὑσπλήγων ἢ τέρματος εἶδέ τις ἄκρου
ἠΐθεον, μέσσῳ δʼ οὒ ποτʼ ἐνὶ σταδίῳ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.706: δένδρεον ἱερόν εἰμι· παρερχόμενός με
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
δένδρεον ἱερόν εἰμι· παρερχόμενός με φυλάσσευ
πημαίνειν· ἀλγῶ, ξεῖνε, κολουομένη.
μέμνεο, παρθένιός μοι ἔπι φλόος, οὐχ ἅπερ ὠμαῖς
ἀχράσιν· αἰγείρων τίς γένος οὐκ ἐδάη;
εἰ δὲ περιδρύψῃς με παρατραπίην περ ἐοῦσαν,
δακρύσεις· μέλομαι καὶ ξύλον Ἠελίῳ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.25: Φοῖβε, Κεφαλλήνων λιμενοσκόπε, θῖνα Πανόρμου
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Φοῖβε, Κεφαλλήνων λιμενοσκόπε, θῖνα Πανόρμου
ναίων, τρηχείης ἀντιπέρην Ἰθάκης,
δός με διʼ εὐπλώτοιο πρὸς Ἀσίδα κύματος ἐλθεῖν,
Πείσωνος δολιχῇ νηὶ συνεσπόμενον
καὶ τὸν ἐμὸν βασιλῆα τὸν ἄλκιμον εὖ μὲν ἐκείνῳ
ἵλαον, εὖ δʼ ὕμνοις ἄρτισον ἡμετέροις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.20: φεύγεθʼ ὅσοι λόκκας ἢ λοφνίδας
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
φεύγεθʼ ὅσοι λόκκας ἢ λοφνίδας ἢ καμασῆνας
ᾄδετε, ποιητῶν φῦλον ἀκανθολόγων,
οἳ τʼ ἐπέων κόσμον λελυγισμένον ἀσκήσαντες,
κρήνης ἐξ ἱερῆς πίνετε λιτὸν ὕδωρ.
σήμερον Ἀρχιλόχοιο καὶ ἄρσενος ἦμαρ Ὁμήρου
σπένδομεν ὁ κρητὴρ οὐ δέχεθʼ ὑδροπότας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.31: οὔ μοι Πληιάδων φοβερὴ δύσις
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
οὔ μοι Πληιάδων φοβερὴ δύσις, οὐδὲ θαλάσσης
ὠρῦον στυφελῷ κῦμα περὶ σκοπέλῳ,
οὐδʼ ὅταν ἀστράπτῃ μέγας οὐρανός, ὡς κακὸν ἄνδρα
ταρβέω, καὶ μύθων μνήμονας ὑδροπότας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.327: τὴν ξηρὴν ἐπὶ νῶτα Λυκαινίδα
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
τὴν ξηρὴν ἐπὶ νῶτα Λυκαινίδα, τὴν Ἀφροδίτης
λώβην, τὴν ἐλάφου παντὸς ἀπυγοτέρην,
αἰπόλος ᾗ μεθύων οὐκ ἄν ποτε, φασί, συνῴκει,
γοῖ, γοῖ. τοιαῦται Σιδονίων ἄλοχοι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.75: Ζηνὶ καὶ Ἀπόλλωνι καὶ Ἄρεϊ
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Ζηνὶ καὶ Ἀπόλλωνι καὶ Ἄρεϊ τέκνον ἀνάκτων
εἴκελον, εὐκταίη μητέρος εὐτοκίη,
πάντα τοι ἐκ Μοιρέων βασιλήια, πάντα τέλεια
ἦλθεν ἐποιήθης δʼ ἔργον ἀοιδοπόλων.
Ζεὺς σκῆπτρον βασίλειον, Ἄρης δόρυ, καλλοσύνην δὲ
Φοῖβος ἔχει· παρὰ σοὶ δʼ ἀθρόα πάντα, Κότυ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.143: Μηδείης τύπος οὗτος· ἴδʼ ὡς
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Μηδείης τύπος οὗτος· ἴδʼ ὡς τὸ μὲν εἰς χόλον αἴρει
ὄμμα, τὸ δʼ εἰς παίδων ἔκλασε συμπαθίην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.184: Αὐσονίῳ Πείσωνι συνασπιστὴς Διόνυσος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Αὐσονίῳ Πείσωνι συνασπιστὴς Διόνυσος
ἵδρυμαι μεγάρων φρουρὸς ἐπʼ εὐτυχίῃ.
ἄξιον, “ὦ Διόνυσ’, ἐσέβης δόμον. ἔπρεπεν ἄμφω,
καὶ μέγαρον Βάκχῳ, καὶ Βρόμιος μεγάρῳ.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.208: ἡ τὰ πέδιλα φέρουσα, Μενεκράτις
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἡ τὰ πέδιλα φέρουσα, Μενεκράτις· ἡ δὲ τὸ φᾶρος,
Φημονόη· Πρηξὼ δʼ, ἣ τὸ κύπελλον ἔχει.
τῆς Παφίης δʼ ὁ νεὼς καὶ τὸ βρέτας· ἄνθεμα δʼ αὐτῶν
ξυνὸν· Στρυμονίου δʼ ἔργον Ἀριστομάχου.
πᾶσαι δʼ ἀσταὶ ἔσαν καὶ ἑταιρίδες· ἀλλὰ τυχοῦσαι
κύπριδος εὐκρήτου, νῦν ἑνός εἰσι μία.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.209: Βιθυνὶς Κυθέρη με τεῆς ἀνεθήκατο
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Βιθυνὶς Κυθέρη με τεῆς ἀνεθήκατο, Κύπρι,
μορφῆς εἴδωλον λύγδινον, εὐξαμένη.
ἀλλὰ σὺ τῇ μικκῇ μεγάλην χάριν ἀντιμερίζου,
ὡς ἔθος· ἀρκεῖται δʼ ἀνδρὸς ὁμοφροσύνῃ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.241: ἡ κόρυς ἀμφοτέρην ἔλαχον χάριν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἡ κόρυς ἀμφοτέρην ἔλαχον χάριν εἰμὶ δʼ ὁρᾶσθαι
καὶ τερπνὴ φιλίοις, καὶ φόβος ἀντιπάλοις.
ἐκ δὲ Πυλαιμένεος Πείσων μʼ ἔχει· ἔπρεπεν ἄλλαις
οὔτε κόρυς χαίταις, οὔτε κόμη κόρυθι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.249: Δαμπάδα κηροχίτωνα, Κρόνου τυφήρεα λύχνον
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Δαμπάδα κηροχίτωνα, Κρόνου τυφήρεα λύχνον,
σχοίνῳ καὶ λεπτῇ σφιγγομένην παπύρῳ,
Ἀντίπατρος Πείσωνι φέρει γέρας· ἢν δὲ μʼ ἀνάψας
εὔξηται, λάμψω φέγγος ἀκουσίθεον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.256: Ταύρου βαθὺν τένοντα, καὶ σιδαρέους
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Ταύρου βαθὺν τένοντα, καὶ σιδαρέους
Ἄτλαντος ὤμους, καὶ κόμαν Ἡρακλέους
σεμνὰν θʼ ὑπήναν, καὶ λέοντος ὄμματα
Μιλησίου γίγαντος οὐδʼ Ὀλύμπιος
Ζεὺς ἀτρόμητος εἶδεν, ἄνδρας ἡνίκα
πυγμὰν ἐνίκα Νικοφῶν Ὀλύμπια,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.335: Καυσίη, ἡ τὸ πάροιθε Μακηδόσιν
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
Καυσίη, ἡ τὸ πάροιθε Μακηδόσιν εὔκολον ὅπλον,
καὶ σκέπας ἐν νιφετῷ, καὶ κόρυς ἐν πολέμῳ,
ἱδρῶ διψήσασα πιεῖν τεόν, ἄλκιμε Πείσων,
Ἡμαθὶς Αὐσονίους ἦλθον ἐπὶ κροτάφους.
ἀλλὰ φίλος δέξαι με· τάχα κρόκες, αἵ ποτε Πέρσας
τρεψάμεναι, καὶ σοὶ Θρῇκας ὑπαξόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.158: αἰάζει πήρη τε, καὶ Ἡράκλειον
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
αἰάζει πήρη τε, καὶ Ἡράκλειον ἄριστον
βριθὺ Σινωπίτου Διογένευς ῥόπαλον,
καὶ τὸ χύδην ῥυπόεντι πίνῳ πεπαλαγμένον ἔσθος
διπλάδιον, κρυερῶν ἀντίπαλον νιφάδων,
ὅττι τεοῖς ὤμοισι μιαίνεται· ἦ γὰρ ὁ μέν που
οὐράνιος, σὺ δʼ ἔφυς οὑν σποδιῇσι κύων.
ἀλλὰ μέθες, μέθες ὅπλα τὰ μὴ σέθεν· ἄλλο λεόντων,
ἄλλο γενειητῶν ἔργον ὄρωρε τράγων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.219: οὐ προσέχω, καίτοι πιστοί τινες
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
οὐ προσέχω, καίτοι πιστοί τινες· ἀλλὰ μεταξύ,
πρὸς Διός, εἴ με φιλεῖς, Πάμφιλε, μή με φίλει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.224: ἑστηκὸς τὸ Κίμωνος ἰδὼν πέος
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
ἑστηκὸς τὸ Κίμωνος ἰδὼν πέος, εἶφʼ ὁ Πρίηπος·
οἴμοι, ὑπὸ θνητοῦ λείπομαι ἀθάνατος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.290: αὐτὸν βακχευτὴν ἐνέδυ θεόν, ἡνίκα
poems.author: Antipater of Thessalonica
poems.text:
αὐτὸν βακχευτὴν ἐνέδυ θεόν, ἡνίκα βάκχας
ἐκ Θηβῶν Ἰταλὴν ἤγαγε πρὸς θυμέλην,
ἀνθρώποις Πυλάδης τερπνὸν δέος, οἷα χορεύων
δαίμονος ἀκρήτου πᾶσαν ἔπλησε πόλιν.
Θῆβαι γιγνώσκουσι τὸν ἐκ πυρός· οὐράνιος δὲ
οὗτος, ὁ παμφώνοις χερσὶ λοχευόμενος.
